<hypothesis>
To distinguish mechanisms, I should vary catalyst concentration significantly. This probes catalyst order:
- M1, M4-M5 standard first-order in cat
- M2, M3, M13 involve cat dimerization (higher order in cat at high loading)
- M6, M8 involve cat activation/ligand dissociation (different cat dependence)
- Deactivation pathways (M9, M13, M19, M20) become more pronounced at different cat levels

Using a high catalyst concentration (e.g., 0.1 M) with same [S]=1.0 will:
- Accelerate dimerization-based deactivation (M2, M3, M13)
- Reveal saturation behavior if binding is strong
- Amplify any cat-squared terms
- Reveal ligand equilibrium effects (M8)

This single perturbation provides broad discrimination among many mechanisms simultaneously because the catalyst-order dependence differs between groups.
</hypothesis>
